title: Model Not Learning (Loss Not Decreasing)
description: Troubleshooting and resolving flat loss curves or stagnant metrics during training. This guide details diagnostic checks, layer-wise gradient flow tests, activation saturation checks, and corrective actions.
name: Model Not Learning (Loss Not Decreasing)

quick_identification.check: Loss curve is flat across multiple epochs
quick_identification.description: Monitor training logs for loss values that do not trend downward.

quick_identification.check: Validation metrics are static or random
quick_identification.description: Accuracy, F1, or task metrics show no improvement over baseline.
Use gradient norm logging to detect vanishing gradient signals.

symptoms.description: Training loss remains constant or oscillates around the same value for many epochs.
symptoms.error_message: No explicit error; loss values are stable but high.
symptoms.where_appears: Training loop, loss computation, optimizer step.

symptoms.description: Model outputs are identical across samples or statistically random.
symptoms.error_message: No explicit error; predictions lack discriminative power.

symptoms.description: Gradient norms are extremely small, indicating no signal backpropagating.
symptoms.error_message: No explicit error; gradient inspection reveals vanishing values.

root_causes.explanation: Insufficient learning rate makes parameter updates too small to escape plateaus or overcome gradient noise; warmup and schedule design matter because learning-rate choice strongly affects early convergence.
recognition_clues: Loss decreases by less than 0.001 per epoch.
Gradients are small but non-zero.
Increasing learning rate causes immediate loss reduction.
root_causes.typical_environment: Fine-tuning pretrained models, conservative hyperparameter choices.

root_causes.explanation: Gradient signals decay through deep stacks, recurrent paths, or saturated nonlinearities, leaving early layers effectively untrained.
recognition_clues: Later layers update normally; early layers have near-zero gradients.
Sigmoid/tanh-heavy deep networks show poor signal flow.
Residual structure or normalization is absent or misconfigured.
root_causes.typical_environment: Very deep networks, RNNs, architectures without residual connections.

root_causes.explanation: ReLU units can become permanently inactive when inputs stay negative, especially after poor initialization or aggressive updates, which blocks useful gradient propagation.
recognition_clues: Large percentage of neurons output zero consistently.
Loss flatlines after an initial decrease.
Replacing ReLU with LeakyReLU resumes learning.
root_causes.typical_environment: Networks with poor initialization, aggressive regularization, or unstable early training.

root_causes.explanation: A mismatch between loss formulation and task can produce weak or misleading gradients, especially with custom reductions, label encoding errors, or framework migration mistakes.
recognition_clues: Loss value is orders of magnitude wrong for the task.
Gradient direction contradicts expected behavior.
Switching loss function immediately changes loss trajectory.
root_causes.typical_environment: Multi-task learning, custom loss implementations, framework version migrations.

root_causes.explanation: Layers may be inadvertently frozen or omitted from the optimizer, so only a subset of the model can adapt.
recognition_clues: Only final layer weights change; backbone is static.
Loss decreases slightly then plateaus at a suboptimal value.
named_parameters() shows no gradient accumulation in intended layers.
root_causes.typical_environment: Transfer learning, feature extraction mode, partial fine-tuning pipelines.

root_causes.explanation: The model may be receiving constant batches, mislabeled examples, collapsed augmentation, or otherwise unlearnable signal, so optimization converges to a trivial baseline.
recognition_clues: Training loss equals validation loss.
Data inspection reveals identical batches or shuffled labels.
Loss is stuck near random-guess baselines.
root_causes.typical_environment: Custom data loaders, distributed sampling bugs, augmentation pipelines that collapse variance.

root_causes.explanation: If accumulated gradients are not normalized by accumulation steps, the effective update scale can become inconsistent and make optimization appear stalled or poorly tuned.
recognition_clues: Loss improves with accumulation_steps=1 but flatlines with larger values.
Effective batch size is large but updates are tiny.
Loss scales with accumulation step count.
root_causes.typical_environment: Large-batch simulation via gradient accumulation, memory-constrained training.

investigation_checklist.description: Verify learning rate is not orders of magnitude too small for the task.
Log gradient norms per layer to detect vanishing gradients.
Inspect intermediate layer outputs for dead neurons or saturation.
Verify loss function matches task and reduction mode is correct.
Verify all intended layers have requires_grad=True and are passed to optimizer.
Inspect batches for label correctness, variance, and shuffling.
Verify gradients are normalized by accumulation steps before optimizer step.

diagnostic_commands.command: for name, param in model.named_parameters(): if param.grad is not None: print(f'{name}: {param.grad.norm().item()}')
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: Early layers with norms near zero indicate vanishing gradients.
High ratios indicate a severe dead ReLU problem.

diagnostic_commands.command: print(f'Optimizer params: {sum(p.numel() for group in optimizer.param_groups for p in group["params"])}')
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: Mismatch indicates frozen layers or missing parameters.
Single label or zero variance indicates pipeline corruption.

diagnostic_tests.test: Run training with learning rate increased by 10x and 100x for 10 steps each.
diagnostic_tests.expected_result: Loss should decrease with higher learning rate until instability appears.
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: If loss remains flat across all rates, cause is not learning rate alone.
diagnostic_tests.next_action: If responsive to higher LR, implement LR warmup and scheduler.

diagnostic_tests.test: Register backward hooks on each layer and log gradient norms.
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: Zero gradients in specific layers indicate vanishing gradients or blocked flow.
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Add residual connections, batch norm, or switch activation functions.

diagnostic_tests.test: Overfit a single batch for 100 steps.
diagnostic_tests.command: for _ in range(100): loss = model(batch); loss.backward(); optimizer.step()
diagnostic_tests.expected_result: Loss should approach zero on a single batch.
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: If loss remains flat, model architecture or loss function is broken; if it overfits, the data pipeline is the issue.
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Fix architecture if the batch cannot overfit; fix data pipeline if it can.

decision_tree.question: Is loss completely flat (no change >1e-4 across epochs)?

yes.question: Are gradient norms near zero across all layers?

yes.result: Dead ReLU / saturated activations — switch to LeakyReLU, check initialization.

no.result: Vanishing gradients — add skip connections, batch norm, or use residual architecture.

yes.result: Learning rate too low — increase by 10x and implement warmup.

no.result: Does overfitting a single batch work?

yes.result: Data pipeline corruption — inspect labels, shuffling, augmentation.

no.result: Incorrect loss function or frozen layers — verify loss-reduction mode and parameter freezing.

no.question: Does loss decrease very slowly (<0.01 per epoch)?

yes.result: Learning rate too low or gradient accumulation not normalized — increase LR or divide accumulated gradients by step count.

no.result: Model is learning normally but converging slowly — consider longer training or curriculum learning.

solutions.permanent_fix: Implement linear warmup from 0 to target LR over the first 10% of steps, then decay.
steps: Identify current learning rate in optimizer configuration.
Increase by a factor of 10 and run 10 steps to verify response.
Implement a warmup schedule followed by decay.
Monitor loss trajectory for sustained decrease.
tradeoffs: Risk of transient instability during warmup.
Requires tuning warmup proportion for different batch sizes.
solutions.performance_impact: No training slowdown; may require 5-10% more steps to converge.
works_for: Fine-tuning scenarios with conservative initial LR.
solutions.verification: Loss should show a consistent downward trend within 50 steps.

solutions.quick_fix: Add normalization after linear or convolution layers.
solutions.permanent_fix: Replace plain architecture with residual blocks; use activation functions with non-zero negative slope.
steps: Inspect gradient norms layer-by-layer to identify where gradients vanish.
Insert batch normalization in affected layers.
Replace ReLU() with LeakyReLU() or GELU().
For deep networks, add residual skip connections every 2-3 layers.
tradeoffs: Residual connections increase memory footprint slightly.
works_for: Deep CNNs and transformers without normalization.
RNNs and LSTMs with long sequences.
solutions.verification: Early-layer gradient norms should become comparable to later-layer norms.

solutions.quick_fix: Replace ReLU with LeakyReLU or PReLU.
solutions.permanent_fix: Use Kaiming/He initialization for layers preceding ReLU; add normalization to prevent distribution shift.
steps: Measure dead neuron ratio per layer using forward hooks.
Replace ReLU() with LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.01) in affected layers.
Reinitialize weights using a ReLU-appropriate scheme.
Add normalization before activation to stabilize input distributions.
tradeoffs: Reinitialization may require restarting training from scratch.
Leaky activations slightly alter model behavior.
works_for: ReLU networks showing a high dead-neuron ratio.
Training runs that flatline after initial decrease.
solutions.verification: Dead neuron ratio should drop sharply within 100 steps.

solutions.quick_fix: Verify loss function matches output activation and task type.
solutions.permanent_fix: Use task-appropriate loss with correct reduction and label encoding.
steps: Confirm classification uses a classification loss with integer labels.
Confirm regression uses a regression loss with float targets.
Verify reduction mode is correct to avoid scale-dependent gradients.
For multi-label tasks, use a loss intended for independent binary targets.
tradeoffs: Changing the loss can require hyperparameter retuning.
Some stable formulations add compute overhead.
solutions.performance_impact: None; correct loss often improves convergence speed.
solutions.verification: Loss should fall into the expected range for the task and begin decreasing reliably.

solutions.solution: Unfreeze Layers and Verify Optimizer Scope
solutions.quick_fix: Pass all intended trainable parameters to the optimizer.
solutions.permanent_fix: Implement staged unfreezing with discriminative learning rates.
steps: List parameters with requires_grad=False.
Set intended layers to trainable.
Rebuild the optimizer with the full trainable parameter set.
For transfer learning, use lower LR for backbone and higher LR for head.
tradeoffs: Full fine-tuning is more expensive and can cause forgetting.
solutions.performance_impact: Full fine-tuning is slower per epoch than feature extraction.
works_for: Transfer learning pipelines stuck in feature-extraction mode.
Models where only the final layer updates.
Distributed training with incorrect parameter synchronization.
solutions.verification: Intended trainable parameters should show non-zero gradient norms after backward pass.

verification_checklist.description: Training loss shows a monotonic or oscillating downward trend.
Accuracy, F1, or task-specific metrics increase over time.

verification_checklist.check: Gradient norms are non-zero in all layers
verification_checklist.description: No layer shows vanishing gradient signal.
Architecture and loss function are capable of memorization.
Output distribution is not uniform or constant.

practices: Start with a learning-rate finder before full training.
Use normalization and residual connections in deep networks.
Overfit a single batch as a sanity check before scaling to the full dataset.
Log gradient norms per layer as a standard training metric.
Implement automatic dead neuron detection alerts.
Use learning-rate warmup as default for jobs with unstable early optimization.
Version-control data preprocessing pipelines to detect corruption.
Track loss curvature to detect plateauing early.
Monitor the train/validation loss gap for optimization and data issues.
Alert when gradient norms fall below a floor for many consecutive steps.
Compare current curves against historical baselines for the same architecture.
Always verify requires_grad status when loading pretrained weights.
Confirm all parameters are present in the optimizer state dict.
Implement data pipeline tests that verify label distribution and batch variance.
Add assertions for loss value ranges and gradient norm floors in training loops.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Flat loss always means the learning rate is too low
common_misconceptions.reality: Vanishing gradients, dead neurons, frozen parameters, and data corruption are equally common causes.

common_misconceptions.misconception: More epochs will eventually fix a flat loss curve
common_misconceptions.reality: If the model cannot learn in a short diagnostic run, more epochs usually just waste compute.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Pretrained models never need learning rate tuning
common_misconceptions.reality: Fine-tuning requires careful LR selection; pretrained weights can mask data and optimizer issues.

false_positive_cases.case: Loss is flat but validation improves
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Validation metrics are improving; training loss may be noisy or regularized.

false_positive_cases.case: Loss decreases slowly due to large dataset
Intentional regularization causing a higher loss floor
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Label smoothing, heavy dropout, or mixup intentionally prevent zero training loss.

escalation_paths.when_to_use: Current architecture is fundamentally incapable of learning the task.
First-order methods consistently fail to escape plateaus or saddle regions.
Task is inherently difficult; model may learn from simplified subtasks.
